speaker: Doctor
text: I see you were in a rear-end collision and are experiencing right groin pain with your leg appearing to be in an abnormal position. Can you tell me if you can move your right foot or toes, and is the pain constant or does it worsen with any specific movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am going to physically examine your right leg to check for instability in the hip joint and any rotational deformity. Please remain still while I gently manipulate the limb to assess for a potential hip dislocation or fracture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The physical findings of shortening, flexion, adduction, and internal rotation strongly suggest a posterior hip dislocation. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a posterior hip dislocation without associated fractures, so we must act quickly to reduce it. I will now attempt a closed reduction of the hip under sedation to restore normal alignment and relieve pressure on the sciatic nerve.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The closed reduction was successful, and the hip is now stable. I need to check for any nerve damage, so can you tell me if you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned earlier that your leg is shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated, which is classic for posterior hip dislocation, but I need to confirm if you have any numbness or weakness in your right foot to rule out sciatic nerve injury. REQUEST TEST: Post-Reduction_Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The post-reduction X-ray is normal, which is excellent news. To rule out a common complication of posterior hip dislocation, please tell me if you have any difficulty extending your foot or if you feel numbness on the outer side of your right foot.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have no signs of nerve injury or further fractures, I can confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
